title: Leader-Member Exchange Quality (Lmx), Telework-Life Conflict, And Professional Isolation: A Gender Moderated Mediation Model
abstract: The present study aims to analyze the mediating role of telework-life conflict in the relationship between LMX and professional isolation in telework and the moderating role of gender in conflict-isolation relationships. A sample of 524 teleworkers (261 women and 263 men) aged 18-67 years (M = 40.54, SD = 9.6) participated in the study. Participants completed a survey assessing LMX, telework-life conflict, and professional isolation. LMX was negatively relatedto telework-life conflict and professional isolation. In addition, the results were consistent with a negative indirect effect of LMX on professional isolation through telework-life conflict (partial mediation). This indirect effect was conditional on gender, such that the positive relationshipbetween conflict and professional isolation was stronger for men than for women. Our findings suggest that high-quality Leader-Member Exchange (LMX) relationships characterized by support, trust, and autonomy are associated with lower feelings of professional isolation.Given the cross-sectional design, these associations should not be interpreted causally. The findings suggest three key practical implications: developing managerial training programs focused on the work-family dynamics of teleworkers; establishing informal communicationspaces that facilitate the negotiation of idiosyncratic deals (i-deals); and implementing HR information systems with a gender perspective that support inclusive organizational policies and reduce gender stereotypes.
